headline: Approved $24,500 Saugatucket Road culvert contract amendment, high school technology contracts, and $44,086.85 library security camera replacement.
summary: Alfred E. Bucco was sworn in as police chief, and five people were appointed to town boards and commissions. Residents spoke about council leadership, the Veolia dispute, and Pond Street traffic.
decisions: Approved the appointment of Alfred E. Bucco as South Kingstown Chief of Police, effective November 9th, 2026.
Approved the appointment of Charles Dickson to the Historic District Commission.
Approved the appointment of C. Stewart to the South Kingstown Veterans Memorial Park Commission.
Approved the appointment of Michaela Barden to the Conservation Commission.
Approved the appointment of William Rosen to the Conservation Commission.
Approved the appointment of David Brown to the Bicycle-Pedestrian Advisory Committee.
Approved a road race license for the Mews Tavern Gear 'N' Beer 5K on November 22nd, 2026, benefiting South County Health.
Approved a Class F 19-hour beverage license for South County Health as beneficiary of the Mews Tavern 5K.
Approved a temporary mass gathering permit for the Whiskey Wonderland at Sons of Liberty, 1425 Kingstown Road, with a rain date of December 19th, 2026.
Approved renewal of the indoor shooting range license for Elite Indoor Gun Range, 371 Rose Hill Road, for the year beginning December 1, 2026.
Approved the final roster of 60 Revolutionary War era Patriots and the inscription wording for the Brave Men as Ever Fought companion memorial.
Approved item 12C, an order of notice for a public hearing.
Approved a $19,500 contract amendment, plus a $5,000 contingency, for Saugatucket Road culvert engineering services, for a total of $24,500.
Approved $44,086.85 to replace library security cameras, plus a $5,000 contingency.
Approved high school technology awards, including network equipment, phones, computer workstations, and security cameras.
Accepted the resignation of Terrence Simpson as registered agent for the Trustees of South Kingstown School Funds, and asked legal counsel to advise on a new agent.
Referred the Pond Street request for a three-way stop sign and more signs to the Town Manager's office.
discussion: Council president selection: Several speakers urged the council to choose the top vote-getter, Deborah D. Bergner, as president. Another speaker said the council should make its own choice.
Pond Street traffic: Residents asked for a three-way stop, more speed limit signs, and enforcement of the no-through-trucks rule. The police chief said trucks had been stopped and some cited.
Polling place numbers: Members discussed whether 11 polling places are needed, given more early and mail-in voting. A report on longer early-voting hours was suggested.
Veolia dispute: Members discussed a meeting with the company next week and whether a closed session was still needed.
Budget meeting dates: Members discussed a joint meeting with the school committee on December 7. Other budget session dates were moved to the next meeting.
